note: People named in the syllabus (guest lecturers, session leads). Everyone listed here also gets a card in the "Guest lecturers" section of /people, in the order below. A week's track lists `people: ["<id>"]` in syllabus.json and the site renders each id as a chip with a hover card, linking to that person's card at /people#<id>. `id` is the slug used from syllabus.json and is the anchor on the People page, so keep it unique and stable. `name` is shown on the chip, including any title (e.g. "Ms Natasha Banks"). `role` and `affiliation` form the line under the name; either may be an empty string. `bio` is a sentence or two. `achievements` is a short list of bullet points (keep to 2-4; an empty list hides the section). `photo` is optional and falls back to initials: put the image in public/people/, named after the id (e.g. public/people/natasha-banks.jpeg), and reference it as "/people/<id>.<ext>". A square headshot of about 400px is plenty; it is only ever shown as an avatar. `href` is optional and points somewhere else on the web that is theirs (LinkedIn, their own site, their employer's staff page); their card on /people shows it as a "More about" link and hides it when absent. It is not their profile on this site: the syllabus chip and the hover card always link to /people#<id>.

people.name: Natasha Banks
people.bio: Natasha (Tash) Banks is the Program Director for Day of AI Australia, a free world-class AI literacy program for teachers and students K-12 across Australia. Her mission is to empower young Australians to confidently shape the AI-powered future. Tash brings over a decade of experience in project management, operations, and stakeholder engagement. She previously served as Head of Operations at Future Women and has held roles at the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC).

people.name: Kenneth Zhang
people.bio: Kenneth builds and ships LLM-powered systems including fine-tuning foundation models, designing RAG and AI agent architectures, and deploying scalable model services as API microservices on Azure and AWS.

people.name: Shurui Li
people.bio: Shurui is a cloud migrations engineer driving initiatives as architect and tech lead to support large-scale customer migrations for Atlassian's server to cloud transition. He focuses on the Extract-Transform-Load streaming pipeline built over Kafka.

people.name: George Ye
people.bio: George Ye leads product at SCX.AI Holdings Limited (ASX-listed), Australia's sovereign AI inference company, where he drives product strategy, model orchestration and customer-facing platform capabilities. Before SCX he held product and data roles at Bigtincan, Westpac, ASIC, CBA and PwC, building large-scale analytics and AI solutions for global enterprise customers. He is a co-inventor on a US patent covering content recommendation technology, and holds degrees from the University of Sydney and Macquarie University.
